report.source_text: The patient was given acetazolamide, aspirin, ocular massage, and a combination of dorzolamide and timolol. She was monitored biweekly to assess visual acuity and intraocular pressure (IOP) for 12 weeks, followed by evaluations every 8 weeks for 6 months, then biannual check-ups for 2 years. At 6 weeks, after resolution of the preretinal hemorrhages, panretinal photocoagulation was performed to prevent neovascular glaucoma, which is associated with central retinal vein occlusion within 90 days. It was performed prophylactically as the patient resides in a remote area and was unwilling to adhere to a regular follow-up schedule. Intravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was not used, as no macular edema was observed on OCT. By the 12th week, the patient’s vision was 6/36, with an IOP of 12 mmHg in the left eye.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) with ciliary retinal artery (CLRA) occlusion secondary to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old Pakistani female presented with sudden, painless vision loss in the left eye (3-hour history) 3.5 months postpartum following cesarean delivery. She had recently used progestin-only pills for 25 days before discontinuing. On examination, she had severe visual impairment (counting fingers at 0.5 feet) with a relative afferent pupillary defect. Fundoscopic examination revealed optic disc edema, 360-degree preretinal hemorrhages, venous dilation and tortuosity, cotton-wool spots, and a white ischemic area nasally to the fovea suggestive of ciliary retinal artery occlusion. OCT showed inner retinal hyperreflectivity, and fluorescein angiography demonstrated delayed dye filling of the ciliary retinal artery with masking from preretinal hemorrhages. Thrombophilia workup was normal, excluding congenital or acquired thrombophilia. The patient was treated with acetazolamide, aspirin, ocular massage, dorzolamide-timolol, and panretinal photocoagulation at 6 weeks. By 12 weeks, visual acuity improved to 6/36 with normal intraocular pressure and no macular edema.
